UPSTREAM: mb/google/hatch: Bump up the BIOS region to 28MiB This change bumps up the BIOS region to 28MiB to use the hole between SI_ALL and SI_BIOS. Since this SPI flash part is 32MiB, only the top 16MiB actually gets memory mapped. Thus, the change ensures that only RW_LEGACY lies in the 12MiB that is not memory mapped. BUG=b:123443737 TEST=Verified that hatch still boots up. Ensured that fmap dump looks correct. UPSTREAM: xhci: A default implementation for Ux timeout calculation and tier policy check As best case, a host controller should support U0 to U1 switching for the devices connected below any tier of hub level supported by usb specification. Therefore xhci_check_tier_policy should always return success as default implementation. A host should be able to issue LGO_Ux after the timeout calculated as per definition of system exit latency defined in C.1.5.2. Therefore xhci_calculate_ux_timeout returns ux_params.sel as the default implementation. Use default calculation in absence of any vendor specific limitations. BUG=b:65034294 TEST=See next commit, this one is dependency Signed-off-by: Pratyush Anand <pratyush.anand@st.com> Tested-by: Aymen Bouattay <aymen.bouattay@st.com> Signed-off-by: Mathias Nyman <mathias.nyman@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org> (cherry picked from commit 9502c46cc9d39330b29d9dc27d8baff4f55d0abc) Signed-off-by: Harry Pan <harry.pan@intel.com> Change-Id: Ibc61ee6f3fc68b145ff10a22d46015a5d00b07b1 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1369448 Commit-Ready: Harry Pan <harry.pan@intel.com> Tested-by: Kyle Williams <kdgwill@chromium.org> Tested-by: Harry Pan <harry.pan@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Kyle Williams <kdgwill@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: xhci: Prevent U1/U2 link pm states if exit latency is too long Don't allow USB3 U1 or U2 if the latency to wake up from the U-state reaches the service interval for a periodic endpoint. This is according to xhci 1.1 specification section 4.23.5.2 extra note: "Software shall ensure that a device is prevented from entering a U-state where its worst case exit latency approaches the ESIT." Allowing too long exit latencies for periodic endpoint confuses xHC internal scheduling, and new devices may fail to enumerate with a "Not enough bandwidth for new device state" error from the host. BUG=b:65034294 TEST=Enable the camera of high bandwidth isochronous transfer, evaluate the kernel do not spit "Not enough bandwidth" error when inserting new USB devices like mouse or usb-storage, and these devices can work as expected. Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> Signed-off-by: Mathias Nyman <mathias.nyman@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org> (cherry picked from commit 0472bf06c6fd33c1a18aaead4c8f91e5a03d8d7b) Signed-off-by: Harry Pan <harry.pan@intel.com> Change-Id: I985c831b00e9a28088e61c29984ce0b1c747b8e6 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1369449 Commit-Ready: Harry Pan <harry.pan@intel.com> Tested-by: Kyle Williams <kdgwill@chromium.org> Tested-by: Harry Pan <harry.pan@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Kyle Williams <kdgwill@chromium.org>

camera: usb: Simplify and fix AE antibanding mode Always use AUTO for ANDROID_CONTROL_AE_ANTIBANDING_MODE. We don't respect ANDROID_CONTROL_AE_ANTIBANDING_MODE in the capture request at all [1], so we might set it to 60Hz based on the current location even if the capture request set it to 50Hz. Changing it to AUTO matches the current behavior better. Note that we still report AUTO even if the underlying camera device does not support setting power line frequency. This is required for CTS [2] and is the behavior of the external camera provider in Android [3]. [1] https://chromium.git.corp.google.com/chromiumos/platform2/+/1bb6d1de9aaf154931fa84c176f3577325714fea/camera/hal/usb/v4l2_camera_device.cc#188 [2] http://cs/android/cts/tests/camera/utils/src/android/hardware/camera2/cts/helpers/StaticMetadata.java?l=568&rcl=5bb489498191a32006744e789a7c8509613c5b00 [3] http://cs/android/hardware/interfaces/camera/device/3.4/default/ExternalCameraDevice.cpp?l=259-262&rcl=afa04bc7d04b0f86056ef813cc0e894251908079 BUG=b:122942809,b:77833131 TEST=Run CameraDeviceTest#testCameraDevicePreviewTemplate with an external camera that does not support setting power line frequency.
